misconception_description: Student believes that a variable assigned an arithmetic expression containing other variables automatically updates its value when those variables change.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahRentang
kamus
  n, awal, akhir, i, x, total : integer
algoritma
  input(n, awal, akhir)
  total <- 0
  input(x)
  total <- total + x
  for i <- 2 to n do
    input(x)
  endfor
  output(total)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes that once they write `sum_range = sum_range + list1[i]`, the variable sum_range is now "linked" to the expression and will automatically update whenever `i` changes. They iterate through the range with the for loop, thinking that as `i` takes on different values, sum_range will automatically accumulate all the values of list1[i]. In reality, sum_range only gets the value of the first element (list1[m]) and never updates, so the function only returns list1[m] instead of the sum of all elements in the range. The student genuinely believes the loop is doing the necessary work by changing i, and that sum_range will track these changes automatically.
